page: Amazon Web Services r6a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by a 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor using the x86_64 architecture, this instance configuration provides 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It delivers 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering an ample 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU (or 16.0 GB per physical core). There is no local ephemeral storage bundled with this instance, requiring external EBS volumes for persistent data. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs included, and baseline network bandwidth is established at 2 Gbps.

Performance profiles exhibit distinct characteristics between single-threaded and parallelized tasks. Single-core compute capability is prominent, demonstrated by a top-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 2976.78 and average results across PassMark CPU and Geekbench single-core metrics. Conversely, multi-threaded throughput falls in the lower tiers across benchmarks such as Geekbench multi-core (3725.0) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, constrained by the physical limit of 2 dedicated execution cores. Memory bandwidth benchmarks yield 38.45 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 22.57 GB/sec for uncached writes, trailing larger scale instances.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the r6a.xlarge serves as a cost-effective allocation of high memory density without paying for redundant compute cores. Workloads that do not require intense parallel compute but rely on sizable working sets benefit from this memory-heavy ratio. Primary use cases include medium-sized in-memory caches, backend Redis or relational databases, ETL pipelines with large buffers, and memory-intensive enterprise web services.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.xlarge is a memory-optimized Nitro instance featuring 4 vCPUs (2 physical cores) powered by a 3.6 GHz AMD EPYC 7R13 processor and 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, catering directly to memory-intensive processes. The instance includes no local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying on networked storage and offering a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks demonstrate solid single-thread performance alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to the low physical core count. Memory bandwidth registers at 38.45 GB/sec for uncached reads. The r6a.xlarge is structurally suited for workloads requiring substantial RAM allocations without heavy multi-core CPU overhead, such as caching tiers, data ingestion pipelines, mid-tier relational databases, and enterprise application servers.

tagline: A high-density memory-optimized cloud instance providing thirty-two gigabytes of RAM across four AMD EPYC vCPUs for memory-intensive workloads.
bullet_points: 4 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 processors clocked at 3.6 GHz
32.0 GB DDR4 system memory providing an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio
Strong single-core processing capability combined with dedicated core threads
Zero bundled local instance storage, requiring remote network storage
Baseline network throughput capacity capped at 2 Gbps
